title: Market morphology and model procurement lifecycle
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Build a compact, operationalized framework that maps market 'morphology' (provider concentration, regional latency footprint, quantization readiness, license friction) to a procurement lifecycle that product, GTM, and procurement teams can use to decide whether to (a) buy hosted, (b) reserve Dedicated, or (c) onboard a Private deployment.
background: We currently surface model availability and cost signals in several ad-hoc dashboards and research docs. Sales/solutions teams ask for a straightforward procurement decision flow tied to risk and latency buckets. The goal is to create a repeatable scoring method, a watchlist cadence, and an actionable doc + minimal console UI mock that reduces ad-hoc decision time for enterprise deals.
tasks: Run 3-week competitive telemetry sweep: latency heatmap (NA/EU/APAC), quantization/FP16 availability, license terms matrix
Interview 6 field reps + 3 enterprise customers about procurement constraints and fallback tolerance
Define 7 procurement triggers (e.g., availability drop >25%, price delta >30%, license change) and map to recommended mitigations
Design friction scoring rubric (technical, commercial, compliance) and prototype 10 sample model scores
Wireframe a lightweight Console panel showing 'Procurement Readiness' and watchlist alerts
Hand off scoring algorithm and data feed spec to Eng (ENG-3110) for automation
acceptance_criteria: Validated scoring rubric: independent reviewers (PM, Sales, Legal) accept scores for at least 10 real models
Deliver a one-page procurement decision flow chart and 2-page executive brief for GTM
Prototype Console mock linked in this ticket and reviewed by Design
Automation spec (data fields, refresh cadence) posted to GitHub repo and assigned to ENG-3110
Watchlist operational cadence documented and owners triaged for Q2 execution

2025-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Post-review notes consolidated. Trade-offs: breadth-first coverage (many models, shallow scoring) vs depth-first (fewer models, inspector-level evidence). Decided: Q2 pilot will focus depth on top 12 models used in enterprise accounts. Remaining models will be on a rotating low-touch watchlist. Added follow-up: schedule 1-hour sync with Sales Ops on 2025-03-04.
links: GitHub draft for scoring rubric and ingestion spec: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-intel/pull/87
notes: Scoring rubric draft uses three pillars: Technical (latency, quant readiness), Commercial (license terms, price delta), Operational (vendor SLA, regional capacity). Each pillar normalized 0-100 and weighted (T:45%, C:30%, O:25%).
Pilot selection heuristic: top 12 models by enterprise token spend + two emerging open models our solutions team is asked about most often.
Measure of success: reduce average procurement decision time for sales motions from 6 days to <=48 hours for pilot use cases.
